name: Malavedan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Bhattacharya 1976 subclassification comment on Glottolog; no phonology/grammar located

sources.citation: Hyrunnisa Beegum, A. 1991. Language of Malavedas. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Kerala, Trivandrum (guide N. Rajendran). c. 405 pp.http://hdl.handle.net/10603/98280
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. I Phonemics p. 41: suprasegmental phonemes = 'two junctures, four pitch levels and three terminals'; sec. 1.5 (pp. 66-75) treats junctures, pitch levels, terminals, sentence and phrase intonation (e.g. numeral/adjective + noun -> higher pitch on the noun); sec. 1.6 syllable structure. No word-stress/accent statement (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence = 0; sections read).

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7), July 2013. Section 10 'Malaveda/Veda', p. 39 ff.
sources.note: Nothing; text identical to the 1996 Encyclopaedia entry (phoneme inventory only).

sources.citation: Gopinathan Nair, B. 2007. Review of B. Ramakrishna Reddy's bibliography of tribal Dravidian languages. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics 36(1): 199-202 (and other IJDL volumes held by the project).
sources.note: Nothing; mentions Malaveda only as a tribal speech tentatively classed as a Malayalam dialect and notes most work on it was done at Univ. of Kerala.

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (chief ed.) 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Article 'MALAVEDA LANGUAGE', pp. 233-236.
sources.note: Nothing. 'The phonemic system is very close to that of Malayalam with the exception that Veda does not have voiced and aspirated stops'; vowel and consonant charts only; rest morphology/lexis.

sources.citation: Radhakrishnan Mallassery, S. 1984. Language of Malavedas. Journal of Tamil Studies 25 (June 1984): 40-49. Madras: International Institute of Tamil Studies.
sources.note: Nothing. 'Phonological peculiarities' 1-9 (pp. 43-44): five vowels, no diphthongs, no voiced/aspirated stops, marginal /s/, interdental lateral /L/, few clusters, 'Monosyllabic words are absent', 'Steep falling terminals are absent'. No stress/accent remark.

sources.citation: Devassy, M. K. 1975. Census of India 1971, Series 9 Kerala, Part V-B(i): Ethnographic Notes on Scheduled Tribes (Hill Pulaya, Malai Vedan, Uraly and Kadar). Malai Vedan monograph, ch. I para 3 and ch. VII 'Language and literature' p. 50.
sources.note: Impressionistic only: 'The mother tongue of the Malai Vedan is a corrupt form of Malayalam with hard intonation and accent'; no locational statement.
